When will the Kingdom of God come?

The common understanding among Jews was that the Messiah would establish God’s Kingdom in Jerusalem; he would defeat Israel’s enemies and bring in a period of peace, prosperity, justice, and righteousness (see
; cp.

). The Pharisees were apparently challenging Jesus’ claim to be the Messiah because he was not defeating the Romans or establishing his Kingdom physically on earth. Jesus did not reject this future manifestation of the Kingdom (see
) but pointed out that the Kingdom of God was being revealed to them through his ministry, though they were missing it. •
The Kingdom of God can’t be detected by visible signs:
Jewish apocalyptic literature of Jesus’ day looked for visible signs in the heavens to signal the coming of the Messiah’s kingdom. Jesus elsewhere affirmed that such signs would appear (see
), but the Pharisees were missing the manifestation of the Kingdom in Jesus’ immediate ministry (cp.
